import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

The commit is declared; the host makes it after this turn ends.

**Order and content**
- The file opens with the title, then a two-sentence research query, then the infographic (`note_goto_double_slash_infographic.png`, which exists beside the report), then `## Bottom line`.
- The bottom line is the lead's verdict: build it, with three corrections, and the second `\` keeps today's behaviour.
- The remaining sections follow the questions a reader would ask: is this a good idea, what exists today, requirement adjustments, keystroke model, note catalog, picker, architecture, risks, open questions, follow-ups, disagreements, sources.
- No headings are numbered and there is no table of contents. The lead's italic byline moved to the top of the Sources section.
- Everything the lead wrote survives: every table cell, number, caveat, open question and source. A word-level comparison found that the only differences are heading wording and the `§` cross-references.
- I replaced the lead's nine `§N` cross-references with in-document links, since those section numbers no longer exist. This changed three table cells (R2, Transport, Query spaces) only by that link.
- The lead's report had no external URLs, so there was nothing to curl and nothing is unrepairable. Its one relative image, `fig-final-keys.png`, exists. All 8 in-document anchors resolve in `pandoc -t html` output.

**Diagrams**
- **Accepted:** `note-goto-grammar-handoff` → `#figure-note-goto-grammar-handoff`. It sits after the paragraph in "The keystroke model" that contains its anchor text. The fence is byte-identical to the manifest's, wrapped with the caption in one figure `<div>`. A single reference sentence that ends that paragraph links to it.
- **Omitted:** none. The manifest proposed only this one diagram; its status was `ready` and its source matched the lead's label.
- The manifest's note above the fence ("Either entry branch can be used…") wasn't copied, because the figure block may hold only the fence and caption.
- There are 1 figure `<div>` and 1 mermaid fence: the lead's report had 0 fences, plus this 1 accepted diagram.
